events.title: A Gift in Motion
events.description: A multidisciplinary showcase from the artists and scholars of the full-time faculty and staff at the Corcoran School of the Arts & Design. A Gift In Motion loosely draws from Robin Wall Kimmerer’s book The Serviceberry which uplifts Indigenous frameworks of the natural world to advance the possibilities in collectivity, reciprocity, and the mindset of abundance. These are anti-capitalist models and theories that provide insight into the systems of power we negotiate, but also offer a lens on how we individually move through our daily lives—together—through historically fraught landscapes. A keen reminder that working with, for, and because of each other remains the most human motivation, even while we are inundated with narratives that suggest otherwise. Within the walls of the academy, frameworks of artistic and creative knowledge are often dismissed, as are Indigenous methodologies and community-focused perspectives that center human engagement, oral and craft-based practices, and unquantifiable research. A personal experience. A feeling. Abstraction. And yet, for centuries, within the walls of art schools exist myriad economies of imagination that are anchored in the sharing of diverse creative knowledge and articulated in what we make, write, perform, dance, build, conserve, collect, display, speak, and think. events.description: Old Glory, reimagined: artists transform our flag over the centuries. Across generations, the Stars and Stripes has inspired pride, protest, and profound artistic expression. This installation features some 30 artworks from the late 1800s to present day, tracing how the meaning of the US flag has evolved over time. events.title: Annapolis Jazz & Roots Festival
events.description: Annapolis Jazz & Roots is launching its fifth festival on the scenic shores of the Chesapeake Bay. Events combine music, art, poetry and history on two weekends, November 6-15. Based in the maritime community of Eastport, the festival includes eight venues in nearby neighborhoods. Each has its own distinct character and charm. Festival goers can visit centuries old buildings, take in restorative bay views and stroll the tree-lined streets of the historic Maryland city. THEME AND HIGHLIGHTS The 2026 theme “New World Music: Centuries of Sound” will be brought home by international and regional performers. An adventurous lineup includes programs rooted in history and culture from colonial days to modern times. Trace the evolution of music and culture since the days Indigenous tribes walked the forests and rode the waters. Gain new insights into the startling history and legacy of slavery and indenture in Maryland; delve into the soulful roots of jazz, and celebrate the changing color of sound in America. Events are free or require modest admission, and all but two venues offer free onsite parking. Reservations are strongly advised for all events. Tickets are sold through instantseats.com. WEEKEND ONE Opening Night takes place Friday, November 6 at 7:00 p.m. at St. Luke’s Episcopal Church in Eastport. Jazz lovers will appreciate how the intimacy and beautiful acoustics of the venue elevate the listening experience when the Muneer Nasser Band performs. Trumpeter Muneer Nasser was exposed to great music by his father, jazz bassist Jamil Nasser. This concert pays homage to three legendary musicians born in 1926: John Coltrane, Miles Davis and Randy Weston. Their brave explorations led to seismic shifts in the sonic landscape and continue to resonate around the globe. On Saturday at 11:00 a.m. visit Eastport-Annapolis Neck Library to gain new insights into slavery and indenture in colonial times. The exhibition is part of a University of Maryland Arts for All-funded project aimed at engaging students in science communication through art, increasing awareness of insect biodiversity and ecological roles, fostering collaboration across disciplines, evaluating changes in attendee knowledge, attitudes, and intentions, and contributing to a replicable arts-based model for conservation education. The exhibition will highlight six Maryland insect species that are included on Maryland’s List of Rare, Threatened, and Endangered Animals . Original works created through the exhibition’s two different open calls will be displayed alongside science-based information about insect ecological roles, insect habitats, and key conservation actions. events.title: Bison: Standing Strong
events.address: 10th St. & Constitution Ave., NW, Washington, DC 20560
events.description: Explore the remarkable story of bison. These iconic animals shaped North American landscapes for more than 100,000 years and anchored Indigenous lifeways for generations. Pushed to the brink of extinction in the 19th century, bison survived thanks to dedicated conservation efforts. Today, they stand strong as an enduring symbol of survival and resilience. The Bison: Standing Strong exhibit invites you into this incredible journey. Explore a full-sized bull bison specimen, the six-foot-wide skull of an ancient bison ancestor, an immersive soundscape, multimedia, cutting-edge scientific research, and Native objects and stories shared in collaboration with community members. Experience the deep history of America’s national mammal and discover the hopeful future being built for generations to come.

events.title: Brady Art Gallery Tour: Unfossilizing African Art and Cracks & Reforms
events.description: Take a student-led tour of the exhibitions currently on view at the Brady Art Gallery: "Unfossilizing African Art" and "Cracks and Reforms". Unfossilizing African Art recontextualizes African material culture objects that have been held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students across four seminar courses conducted original research to deepen understanding of the collection and reconsider how these objects are interpreted and exhibited. Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection examines a decade shaped by political upheaval, social transformation, migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition. This exhibition, developed as part of an art history class taught by Associate Professor Bibi Obler, is accompanied by a catalog designed by graphic design students.

events.title: Bronze Bison: Exhibit
events.address: 10th St. & Constitution Ave., NW, Washington, DC 20560
events.description: More than 100 years ago, real bison grazed outside the Smithsonian Castle building. Bison are returning in a bold new way! Three larger-than-life bronze bison, created by sculptor Gary Staab, find a permanent home outside the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History. These towering sculptures of a bull, cow, and calf are at 125 percent scale and modeled after taxidermy specimens seen at the Smithsonian between 1888 and 1957. The original bison diorama introduced generations of visitors to an animal and a prairie landscape they had never seen and helped spark the bison conservation movement. The new bison bronzes will welcome visitors from around the world and celebrate America’s national mammal. Gift of Naoma Tate and the family of Hal Tate.

events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.

Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

Blanton and her road-tested band deploy humor, camaraderie, and considerable musical muscle to enroll each audience in a rare vision of hope and solidarity. In addition to writing and performing music, Carsie works as a political organizer and activist. The Little Flame features background vocals from Irish band Ye Vagabonds and Carsie’s Palestinian/New Zealander prison-mate Rana Hamida, and appears on her latest album, The Red Album Vol II. events.description: Greater Oakton Community Association invites history enthusiasts to join a narrated historic bus tour led by acclaimed local historian Jim Lewis on from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. Please arrive at 9:00 a.m. at Oakton Community Park at 2841 Hunter Mill Road (next to the old schoolhouse and roundabout) for Jim Lewis's opening comments, then board the bus for departure by 9:30 a.m. The tour will end at 1:00 p.m. This 3.5-hour journey spans Fairfax County's history from its formation in 1742 through the early 1900s, focusing on sites primarily on or just off Hunter Mill Road. Participants hear stories of where the old mills and roads were located and learn about famed military figures (particularly from the Civil War era) and colorful residents who graced the area. events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. events.title: Emancipation Proclamation Rotunda Display
events.description: For the first time since 1952, the National Archives welcome new, permanent document cases in the Rotunda as it unveils the original 1863 Emancipation Proclamation signed by Abraham Lincoln. While the Founding Documents—the Declaration of Independence, U.S. Constitution, and Bill of Rights—established the nation’s path during the revolutionary and colonial period, the addition of the Emancipation Proclamation to the Rotunda demonstrates the nation’s continued journey to expand rights to its citizens.

events.title: Entertainment Nation
events.address: 14th Street and Constitution Avenue, N.W., Washington, DC 20560
events.description: Entertainment has the power to captivate, inspire and transform us. It brings us together. We share it when we spontaneously recite lines from a favorite movie, dance to the same groove or recreate a national sports moment on a neighborhood street. It can also spur critical conversations, expose divides, and foster important historical change. Through the National Museum of American History’s extraordinary collection of theater, music, sports, movie and television objects, the exhibition features a powerful, ever-changing selection of objects and interactive experiences. Through the objects and their stories, the exhibition explores how, for more than 150 years, entertainment has provided a forum for important national conversations about who we are, and who we want to be.

events.title: Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY
events.description: For Freedoms presents artist and educator Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY which centers on Ethiopian journalist and author Baalu Girma’s controversial 1984 Amharic novel Oromay, written under the Derg regime and banned shortly after its publication. Drawing on Gottesman’s deep engagement with the novel, NIGHT AND DAY considers how artists create, communicate, and sustain cultural memory within and against conditions of censorship, political repression, and state violence. The exhibition extends beyond the gallery through a library of banned books, a self-guided workshop station that invites visitors to respond to censorship through writing and drawing, and a public conversation on how artists sustain creative practice amid sociopolitical pressure.

Weather permitting, we’ll even head outside for a fiber burn test to see fabric identification in action. We’ll also touch on how fiber content affects the way fabric behaves in a garment. You’ll discover why different fabrics work better for different types of projects, how to recognize them, and where to find them. This class is designed to provide a daytime introductory course option to the community. It is perfect for anyone looking to increase their ability to navigate and handle the fabrics they sew, anyone curious about sewing, homeschool students looking for outside instruction, or for those who have not sewn in years and would benefit from a guided refresher. This fabric course is designed to complement other Sew It Begins classes. Look for Fabric Fundamentals 2: Tools, Techniques, and Care.

events.title: Forces of Nature with violinist Francesca Anderegg
events.venue: Maryland Hall for the Creative Arts
events.description: ANNAPOLIS SYMPHONY ORCHESTRA FORCES OF NATURE Friday, November 6, 2026 Saturday, November 7, 2026 6:30 PM Pre Concert Lecture 7:30 PM Concert At Maryland Hall MUSIC PROGRAM Luke Soneral An Overture: The Mouse and its Shadow Reinaldo Moya Vestido de Mar, with violinist Francesca Anderegg Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky The Tempest, Op. 18 Igor Stravinsky Divertimento from Le baiser de la fée (The Fairy’s Kiss) This concert is approximately 2 hours in length, with a 20 minute intermission. In Forces of Nature, the natural world becomes a source of wonder, reflection, and transformation. Emerging composer Luke Soneral opens the program with An Overture: The Mouse and Its Shadow, offering an exciting glimpse of orchestral music’s future. Reinaldo Moya’s ocean-inspired violin concerto, Vestido de Mar, brings violinist Francesca Anderegg to the stage for a work that reflects the landscapes and experiences of the Americas. Tchaikovsky’s The Tempest turns Shakespeare’s storm into a powerful exploration of human nature, while Stravinsky’s The Fairy’s Kiss honors Tchaikovsky through the wintry world of Hans Christian Andersen. Together, these works reveal nature as both an elemental force and a mirror of our inner lives.

Along the way, learn about the soldiers who lived and worked here and the challenges they faced while stationed in the field. At the fort, explore the earthworks that still stand today and imagine what life was like inside this military post. Rangers will share stories of daily routines, military strategy, and the experiences of those who served here. This hike offers a chance to experience history where it happened while connecting with the natural landscape that surrounds it. This program begins at the Rock Creek Park Nature Center.

As Founder & CEO of Silicon Valley Innovations, she leads a world-class team developing first-in-class drug delivery platforms in nasal and feminine healthcare - bringing novel solutions like NasoClenz, the first intranasal antiseptic for consumers, to market. Her ventures have achieved multiple successful exits totaling nearly $500 million, including Hologic’s $125M acquisition of Focal Therapeutics. A holder of 50+ U.S. patents and a member of the Forbes Business Council, Dr. Lebovic has earned global recognition for her pioneering contributions to medicine and innovation. Recent accolades include the 2023 Women in Innovation Award for Leadership, Gold Stevie Award for Female Innovator of the Year (2023), and the Pathfinder Lifetime Achievement Award, joining the ranks of international medical pioneers. Driven by creativity and compassion, Lebovic continues to design products that are intuitive, accessible, and life-changing - bridging the gap between clinical excellence and everyday usability. events.title: Friends Gather Here: A Legacy of Two Communities at Woodlawn
events.description: Friends Gather Here: A Legacy of Two Communities at Woodlawn explores the powerful history of Quaker families who came to Woodlawn to establish an antislavery community rooted in equality and nonviolence. Through innovative farming and free labor, they sought to demonstrate an alternative to slavery in Virginia, settling alongside a small, established free Black community already living in the area. This exhibit examines the parallel lives, shared aspirations, and evolving relationships between these neighboring communities. As part of the Virginia 250th commemoration, Friends Gather Here invites us to reflect on this quiet revolution and examine our nation’s foundational ideals. On View: June 27 – December 30, 2026 Admission: Free (with suggested donation)

events.title: From Consuming to Contributing: How We Built the Space That Was Missing
events.description: Hear from GW Engineering alumnus, Saquib Saifee, M.S. '23, at OWASP Global AppSec USA in San Fransciso, CA! On November 6, he, Caroline Lee, and Gaurang Deshpande from IBM will be leading the panel, "From Consuming to Contributing: How We Built the Space That Was Missing." Many of us naturally drift from consuming OWASP resources to contributing to them. At some point, you stop just reading the Top 10 and start showing up at a chapter, submitting a pull request, or volunteering at a conference. But what often gets lost is the "together" part. The shared strategy, the mutual encouragement, a place where experienced contributors can mentor others and people new to contributing can find their footing without having to figure it out alone. It started when two of us ran into each other at the Boston Application Security Conference. Same organization, same department, had no idea the other was there. That conversation grew into three people, then a cross-regional group, and eventually an initiative with executive sponsorship built around a simple question: what if there was a structured space where people at all levels of OWASP engagement could come together, share what they know, coordinate where to show up, and help each other go deeper? That is what we built. A space where seasoned contributors have a home for their work and a way to pass it on, and where people curious about OWASP but not sure where to start can learn, get mentored, and take their first real steps. Contribution

events.title: Gaelic Storm
events.description: It’s hard to imagine a band just coming into their own after 20 years of success, but that’s exactly what makes a true anomaly. Gaelic Storm, a multi-national, Celticjuggernaut grows stronger with each live performance, and after two decades and over 2000 shows, they are a true force to be reckoned with. The band attributes their continued success to their fanatic audience, and it’s a well-diversified crowd for sure – attracting fans of every genre with their richstorytelling, energetic instrumentals, devotion to Celtic traditions and passion for their stagecraft. They are as loyal to their fans as the fans are to them, as frontman Patrick Murphy states, “The fans are the ones that have given us this life. We’re here for them.” Gaelic Storm takes a true blue-collar, hard-nose approach to touring, consistently traveling the US and internationally forging a unique path in the Celtic musicworld. “You have to see us live. We are the true working-man’s’ band,” says longtime member Ryan Lacey. “We still, and most likely always will, tour most of theyear, and that’s how we constantly hone our craft.” This dedication to their live show dates all the way back to the mid-1990s, when Gaelic Storm kicked off its’ career as a pub band in Santa Monica, California. Onewhich performance led to their discovery that ultimately found the band appearing in the blockbuster film, Titanic (where they performed “Irish Party in ThirdClass”). This laid the groundwork for a career that would eventually find them topping the Billboard World Chart six times, making appearances at mainstreammusic festivals, and regularly headlining the largest Irish Festivals across the country, all while gaining a reputation as a genre-bending Irish rock band whosesongs mix Celtic traditions with something uniquely creative. Recent years have seen the addition of Natalya Kay on fiddle and Parker Hastings on guitar, who both bring their own energy, musicianship and spirit to GaelicStorm.

events.title: Gallery B Presents "Intersections | Realism & Abstraction"
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman - with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details. November 6, 2026 – November 29, 2026 Gallery Hours: Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, 12 – 5pm Opening Reception: Friday, November 6; 6 – 9pm

events.title: In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness
events.address: 14th Street and Constitution Avenue, N.W., Washington, DC 20560
events.description: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History will lead the nation’s 250th anniversary celebrations with a bold, immersive exhibition exploring the ideals of the Declaration of Independence. In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness will span three floors and 300,000 square feet, featuring 250 significant objects, including the desk Jefferson used to draft the Declaration of Independence. Another noteworthy artifact is the only surviving ship of the early U.S. Navy, the gunboat Philadelphia . This National Historic Landmark helped stall British forces and now will undergo an on-site conservation to preserve it for future generations. Visitors and online audiences can engage with both the triumphs and challenges of America’s journey through a year-long series of dynamic programs, from hands-on activities and theatrical performances to educational tools and virtual field trips for classrooms across the country. The museum's Semiquincentennial exhibitions and events begin in the spring of 2026, welcoming all Americans to reflect on the enduring and sometimes delayed or denied promises that surround the ongoing pursuit of life, liberty and happiness.

events.title: Meet Pacific Prep: Free One-on-One Conversations for Families in NOVA
events.description: The Admissions Team is coming to Tysons on Friday, November 6, and we would love to sit down with you and your family. Pacific Preparatory is a Cognia-accredited online K-12 school. Every student learns through 1:1 live instruction that is built around that child, rather than asking the child to fit a school environment. Families can enroll full-time, add a single course, or work with our tutors for academic support, test prep, and enrichment. Our small team of real people takes the time to get to know each student well. We tend to be a good fit for students who have not been well served by traditional school. That includes kids with learning differences, kids who need more flexibility in how and when they learn, and kids who are ready to move faster than their classroom allows. events.title: Miguel Braceli: UNBURIAL (exhibition)
events.address: St. John's College, 60 College Avenue, Annapolis, MD 21401
events.description: Unburial treats absence as a site for learning and reflection. The void left by the Liberty Tree becomes more than metaphor: an art intervention transforms it into a place to be repurposed and reclaimed through rituals and celebrations that probe what freedom means today. On the front lawn, where the Liberty Tree once stood, the artist Miguel Braceli has installed a 40'-diameter circle of cemetery vases filled with common wildflowers. It calls attention to the tree's absence and reclaims it as a tree for all people, not just the privileged and elite (e.g., the Sons of Liberty and the four Annapolis signers of the Declaration of Independence). In the museum, Braceli, with the help of a team of fabricators, created three enormous murals and two other works. The murals perform an autopsy of the tree. The largest multiplies the tulip poplar's distinctive leaf shape across a 33'-long wall in a wind-swept swirl of energy (the leaves were made from stencils of the Liberty Tree scion's actual leaves). A second mural abstracts the tree's tangled root system into a water-bearing drawing (using PVC tubing) that sprouts purple carnations. The third mural's subject is the tree's massive trunk, which was cut to pieces in 1999, with much of the wood later finding commemorative as Liberty Tree guitars, conference tables, and bible boxes. Onto nine chalkboards, Braceli has mounted nine pieces of raw wood, each supporting live orchids. What can we learn anew from this tree?, it seems to ask. The two other works urge us to turn away from nation-state identities and to look and listen more closely to nature. A sculptural ear is mounted onto the red silhouette of a rose petal, borrowed from the work of Columbia-born, Venezuela-based artist Roberto Obregoń. Nearby, a flag of yellow roses hangs from a flagpole that has been fabricated from a branch. Admission & Hours Free & open to the public Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Open Friday, 12 to 7:30 p.m. Parking

This Pulitzer Prize-finalist comedy by Kristoffer Diaz body-slams the world of pro-wrestling, pop culture, and the performance of identity. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

The goal is not simply to experience the work in the room, but to give you the knowledge, tools, and quality ingredients to make it part of your own evening ritual. No prior experience is needed. events.title: Shifting Boundaries: Perspectives on American Landscapes
events.address: Jefferson Drive at 12th St., SW, Washington, DC
events.description: American painters Willard Metcalf, Dwight Tryon, Winslow Homer, and Abbott Thayer created profoundly beautiful views of the New England landscapes where they lived and worked. These paintings largely depict that environment as timeless and static. Shifting Boundaries looks at these works from a new angle by engaging a multiplicity of voices and viewpoints to explore what these paintings can tell us about changes to this region both past and present. As Shifting Boundaries reveals, the views these artists created of pasturelands in Massachusetts and of seascapes in Maine were transforming even as these artists recorded them. This reshaping of landscapes has only accelerated in the century since Metcalf, Tryon, Homer, and Thayer depicted them. Shifting Boundaries pilots a new mode of collaborative curatorial practice. NMAA Lunder Curator of American Art Diana Greenwold , curatorial assistant Mary Mulcahy , and interpretation specialists Liz Gardner and Amy Freesun partnered with Lauren Brandes (Smithsonian Gardens), Dennis Chestnut (Groundwork Anacostia River DC), Jerome Foster II (Waic Up), Elizabeth James-Perry (Aquinnah Wampanoag artist), Lorette Picciano (Rural Coalition), Stephanie Toothman (National Park Service), and Melinda Whicher (Smithsonian Gardens) to develop the themes for this exhibition, select works of art, and write object labels. The group’s perspectives, drawn from their individual areas of professional expertise and their own personal experiences, allow us to see new details in these stunning works of art. The landscapes become invitations to explore a century of human impact on New England land and water, the erasure of indigenous histories, and the environmental changes that are altering this region today.

events.description: The GW Department of Statistics presents, An Overview of LLMs for Statisticians: Foundations, Reasoning, and Agentic AI, a short course taught by Linjun Zhang, associate professor in the Department of Statistics and an affiliated faculty member in computer science at Rutgers University Location: Please note that the location has been updated. Morning Session: Duques Hall, Room 251Afternoon Session: Phillips Hall, Room 411 Date/Time: November 6, 2026 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Lunch break: 12:00–1:30 p.m. Description: This short course provides an overview of the foundations and frontiers of modern large language models (LLMs), with an emphasis on topics relevant to statisticians and data scientists. We will begin with the basic principles underlying embeddings, transformers, and the LLM training pipeline, including pretraining, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning from human feedback. Building on these foundations, we will discuss recent developments in reasoning models and agentic AI, including context engineering, harness engineering, and the design of AI agents for complex tasks. We will also discuss key issues in AI safety, reliability, and evaluation. The short course will combine conceptual foundations with practical examples and hands-on activities, with the goal of helping participants understand, use, and critically evaluate modern AI systems. events.title: The American Story
events.description: The National Archives Museum debuts a once-in-a generation redesign of its permanent exhibits: The American Story and the Discovery Center - connecting visitors with the National Archives in revolutionary ways. The American Story will showcase items and records in the National Archives that tell important moments in our nation's history. Visitors will get up close to more than 40 original artifacts and documents, including a rare 1823 Stone Engraving of the Declaration of Independence, George Washington's annotated copy of the Constitution, and presidential gifts including horseshoes to President Bush from Queen Elizabeth II. The American Story will be the first and only museum in Washington, DC to use artificial intelligence (AI) to bring each visitor a special, individualized opportunity to explore the records of the American people and engage with American history. This exhibit brings more than two million historic records to life, offering a personalized journey through our nation's past. This new museum experience provides all Americans with a special opportunity to celebrate the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.

events.title: Unfossilizing African Art
events.description: Presented after extensive research, this exhibition recontextualizes African material culture objects held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. Image: Once Known Mende carver [Mende, Sierra Leone], Sowei, 19th-20th century, wood, varnish, 16 H x 10 W x 10 D in. Gift of Stephen A. Spear, 1975 (P.75.2.30)

events.title: We Make History
events.description: As the nation commemorates 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence, "We Make History" explores how history happens, is preserved and shared. In Washington, D.C. and places around the country, many people were quietly keeping the records, building the collections, and developing the skills that would create America’s historical narrative. These community-based stories serve as the building blocks for 250 years of American history. Using the country’s anniversary as a milestone, the museum uses its community driven practice to celebrate local civic engagement and encourage local history keeping. This exhibition is a tribute to celebrating our communities and making possible a better understanding of our shared past. These stories are important to marking the Semiquincentennial because they help show the legacy of how people make history one act, one document, one story at a time. By bringing these stories to the forefront in 2026, the exhibit inspires the next generation to keep and share their own stories and records to add to America’s historical narrative. We Make History has an anticipated opening date of May 30, 2026.

events.title: 250 Years of America
events.description: From the stirring opening call of Copland’s Fanfare for the Common Man to the irresistible exuberance of Sousa’s The Stars and Stripes Forever , this program travels through a distinctly American musical landscape. Along the way, you’ll hear the open-hearted simplicity and rhythmic vitality of Copland, the sweeping drama of Richard Rodgers’ Victory at Sea , the patriotic brilliance of Morton Gould’s American Salute , and the rich Romanticism of George Whitefield Chadwick’s Symphony No. 3. Arrive early for a special pre-concert performance by RCO’s principal strings featuring chamber music by Chadwick—a more intimate introduction to one of America’s important early orchestral voices. Bold, lyrical, nostalgic, and unmistakably American, this is a celebration 250 years in the making. Program Aaron Copland – Fanfare for the Common Man Aaron Copland – Hoedown, from the ballet, Rodeo Aaron Copland – Variations on a Shaker Melody, from Appalachian Spring Richard Rogers – Victory at Sea Morton Gould – American Salute George Chadwick – Symphony #3 John Phillip Sousa – Stars and Stripes Forever Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: A Gift in Motion
events.description: A multidisciplinary showcase from the artists and scholars of the full-time faculty and staff at the Corcoran School of the Arts & Design. A Gift In Motion loosely draws from Robin Wall Kimmerer’s book The Serviceberry which uplifts Indigenous frameworks of the natural world to advance the possibilities in collectivity, reciprocity, and the mindset of abundance. These are anti-capitalist models and theories that provide insight into the systems of power we negotiate, but also offer a lens on how we individually move through our daily lives—together—through historically fraught landscapes. A keen reminder that working with, for, and because of each other remains the most human motivation, even while we are inundated with narratives that suggest otherwise. Within the walls of the academy, frameworks of artistic and creative knowledge are often dismissed, as are Indigenous methodologies and community-focused perspectives that center human engagement, oral and craft-based practices, and unquantifiable research. A personal experience. A feeling. Abstraction. And yet, for centuries, within the walls of art schools exist myriad economies of imagination that are anchored in the sharing of diverse creative knowledge and articulated in what we make, write, perform, dance, build, conserve, collect, display, speak, and think. events.title: All Aboard the Historic Sydenstricker Schoolhouse OPEN HOUSE!
events.description: Join us for our monthly Open House featuring a special exhibit: Engines of Progress: Innovation and Trains . Discover how railways revolutionized travel and explore the clever problem-solving—including work by local inventors—that made the tracks safer and better. As an added feature, the Washington, Baltimore & Annapolis Chapter of the Train Collectors Association will have an operating layout in the Schoolhouse. Train Layout & Fun: Get an up-close look at this operating model train layout. Young engineers can put on an engineer's hat, sound the bell and whistle, and blow the horn! Plus, Final Bidding: Place your final bids on a vintage, fully furnished Magnuson "Queen Victoria" dollhouse. Designed by renowned model railroad pioneer Robert Lunde (of Lunde Studios and Magnuson Models), this 1:12 scale masterpiece features his iconic, handcrafted resin-cast brickwork and intricate traditional architecture. Bidding officially closes at 2 PM today! Can’t make it in person? You can view photos, watch a video tour, and place your online bid here: www.sydenstrickerschoolhouse.org/dollhouse/ All auction proceeds directly benefit our upcoming 100th birthday schoolhouse restoration work. Thank you for supporting local history!

events.title: Basia Bulat
events.description: With an electrifying voice and lyrics like silver arrowheads, Basia Bulat has become one of Canada's most conspicuous talents. Juno nominated and short-listed for the prestigious Polaris Music Prize, she often appears solo in gigantic halls, winning over crowds with an autoharp or charango, stomping feet and two mighty lungs. Her massive talent has also been recognized at scale: her songs have been adapted for major performances with symphony orchestras, and she’s been tapped for prestigious tributes to Leonard Cohen and The Band. Since releasing her debut in 2007, she has shared a stage with artists including Arcade Fire, The National, Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds, Daniel Lanois, St Vincent, Sufjan Stevens, Destroyer and Andrew Bird. Bulat was born in Toronto and grew up listening to her mother’s piano students, Sam Cooke and Stax on the oldies station. In early 2016 she released, Good Advice, produced by Jim James of My Morning Jacket.

events.title: Brady Art Gallery Tour: Unfossilizing African Art and Cracks & Reforms
events.description: Take a student-led tour of the exhibitions currently on view at the Brady Art Gallery: "Unfossilizing African Art" and "Cracks and Reforms". Unfossilizing African Art recontextualizes African material culture objects that have been held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students across four seminar courses conducted original research to deepen understanding of the collection and reconsider how these objects are interpreted and exhibited. Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection examines a decade shaped by political upheaval, social transformation, migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition. This exhibition, developed as part of an art history class taught by Associate Professor Bibi Obler, is accompanied by a catalog designed by graphic design students.

events.title: Breathwork on the Farm
events.description: What: A regenerative morning of breathwork Where: The Studio at Honey’s Farmhouse (5819 Brooks Woods Road, Lothian MD 20711) When: Saturday November 7, 2026, 10am-12pm Instructor: Trish Brewer, Certified Breathwork Coach Release, reset, and restore through the breath. Join Certified Breathwork Coach Trish D. Brewer for a Breathwork Circle at the Studio at Honey's Farmhouse and discover how our breath offers us the regenerative power to restore what has been wounded or is inactive within us.⁣ Whether you are new to breathwork or have practiced many times, all welcome. Please read and sign Trish Brewer's Client Introduction & Informed Consent form before you purchase your ticket. About Breathwork: Active Breathwork is a technique that allows you to disconnect from the thinking mind and enter a different state of consciousness. This type of Breathwork can lessen anxiety, depression, and stress. It can release emotional or mental blocks, constriction, tension, trauma, fear, grief, and/or anger.⁣⁣ What to Bring: Yoga mat and/or blanket(s) Eye covering (a bandanna or scarf will do, something to block the light) A journal to write in after Water to sip on before and after Please Note: Breathwork can stir up deep emotions with the intention of lightening things up for you, but it can also be a lot to navigate. It is always my intention to create nurturing and compassionate space.⁣ Consult a doctor before participating in breathwork if you are pregnant, have been diagnosed with cardiovascular disease, suffer from high blood pressure, epilepsy, glaucoma, retinal detachment, aneurysms, osteoporosis, have had recent surgery, or physical injury, have a history of severe mental illness or panic attacks.⁣ Before you purchase, please read and sign Trish Brewer’s Client Introduction & Informed Consent form. This is required for all attendees before every Breathwork Circle. One ticket per attendee is required. Tickets are nonrefundable and nontransferable.

events.title: Camp One Heartland
events.description: Camp One Heartland is a solo exhibition by Tye DuSold-O’Connor archiving documentation of one of the world’s first nonprofit summer camps designated to supporting and empowering youth affected by HIV and AIDS, eventually transforming into a vital beacon of safety, liberation and eutopia for LGBTQ+ youth across the country. After its inaugural session in the summer of 1993 and many more held at different campsites across the country, Camp One Heartland found its permanent residence in Willow River, Minnesota. Over the next three decades it broadened its reach to provide summer camp sessions for youth experiencing housing instability, LGBTQ+ youth, and specifically trans youth. Tye attended Camp One Heartland as both a camper in 2022 and a counselor in 2024, and found these experiences indescribably transformative to them and their queer identity. Quite suddenly, Camp One Heartland shut down permanently in the fall of 2024 due to financial issues. Former campers, counselors and staff have been unable to return to the site since. While camp counseling in the summer of 2024, Tye took hundreds of photos of the camp, its people, and its experiences. These serve as some of the last images taken during the lifetime of Camp One Heartland. events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.

events.description: 8 performances | October 31 and November 6*, 7, 13, and 14 at 7:30pm | November 1, 8, and 15 at 2:00pm *Friday, November 6 will include ASL interpretation and free tickets for Montgomery County residents! Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. events.description: For Freedoms presents artist and educator Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY which centers on Ethiopian journalist and author Baalu Girma’s controversial 1984 Amharic novel Oromay, written under the Derg regime and banned shortly after its publication. Drawing on Gottesman’s deep engagement with the novel, NIGHT AND DAY considers how artists create, communicate, and sustain cultural memory within and against conditions of censorship, political repression, and state violence. events.description: Exhibition Openings: FOCUS at The Delaplaine Saturday, November 7 • 3–5 pm FREE View exhibitions and meet the artists! These exhibitions are opening on Saturday, November 7 and can be viewed starting at 9 am. Beat the crowds and visit us earlier in the day! Nov 7–29 National Juried Photography Exhibition Part of FOCUS: A Celebration of Photography, the NJPE takes place every other year in November. The exhibition features selected photographs by regional and national artists. ABOUT THE JUROR: E. Brady Robinson is a Baltimore-based photographer and creative director known for her vibrant and eclectic mix of fine art photography, cultural documentation, and portraits of creatives. Her work has been featured in solo and group exhibitions in the US and internationally, and her photographs are held in the permanent collections of the Orlando Museum of Art and the Spanish Cultural Center in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. Robinson teaches photography and senior seminar at Georgetown University and is a contributing photographer for BmoreArt and Baltimore Beat. Nov 7–29 Mark Seaver Beauty Through Thin Ice Photography Seaver’s photography uses ice and its properties as a filter through which to photograph. The result is the refraction of light, which distorts and abstracts the world seen through it. Nov 7–29 Christophe Casamassima The Dirty Window Photography The Dirty Window is a phantasmagoric cycle of photography that aligns with the four stages of sleep. Casamassima uses photography to explore how repetition reveals difference and where latent images surface to consciousness before dissolving again. Nov 7–29 Kevin Stivers Elsewhere Photography Elsewhere exists between places, neither here nor there. The work in Stiver’s exhibition explores themes of human connection and disconnect and feelings of belonging and misplacement, shrouded in a surreal atmosphere.

events.title: FACETED Seminar Series | Hand Sculpted: The Art & Evolution of Engraving
events.description: Join the InBloom team on Saturday, November 7th at 3PM in their Downtown Frederick gallery for the next talk in the FACETED seminar series— Hand Sculpted: The Art & Evolution of Engraving . A hand-engraved line isn’t simply applied to jewelry—it deliberately transforms the metal. For centuries, engravers have cut controlled lines into metal to preserve names, create intricate patterns, and bring surfaces and stories to life through texture, light, and shadow. It’s a beautiful expression of InBloom Jewelry’ philosophy: artistry in service to love. Whether a meaningful date inside a band, a name rendered in script, or a hand-cut design inspired by a personal story, hand engraving makes jewelry deeply personal and enduring—meticulously carved by a person, for a person (or by the InBloom goldsmiths, for you). This seminar will include a fascinating discussion on the history and evolution of hand engraving and a live demonstration of this centuries-old art form. Free to all, RSVPs encouraged.

events.title: Forces of Nature
events.description: In Forces of Nature , the natural world becomes a source of wonder, reflection, and transformation. Emerging composer Luke Soneral opens the program with An Overture: The Mouse and Its Shadow , offering an exciting glimpse of orchestral music’s future. Claire Lewis will guest conduct. Reinaldo Moya’s ocean-inspired violin concerto, Vestida de mar (Clothed by the sea) , brings violinist Francesca Anderegg to the stage for a work that reflects the landscapes and experiences of the Americas. Tchaikovsky’s The Tempest turns Shakespeare’s storm into a powerful exploration of human nature, while Stravinsky’s The Fairy’s Kiss honors Tchaikovsky through the wintry world of Hans Christian Andersen. Together, these works reveal nature as both an elemental force and a reflection of our inner lives. The 6:30 PM pre-concert lecture, featuring an interview by Soneral and Moya by WBJC's Jonathan Palevsky, is included in the ticket.

events.title: From Greece to the Levant: An Afternoon of EVOO, Wine, & Mezza
events.description: Immerse yourself in Mediterranean culture tasting the world’s most-awarded Greek olive; sipping wines of the Levant; and dining on a feast prepared by local chef and Dame Nura Mendez of Sahtain Nunu. Celebrate Greek heritage while enjoying the first tastes of the just-arrived new harvest from the Laconiko groves on the sapphire shores of the Peloponnese. Learn about and taste Greek wines from expert Sotiris Bafitis, and experience a cooking demonstration of Levantine cuisine followed by lunch prepared by Chef Nura. The journey begins with a welcome drink from the Laconiko cellars followed by a presentation about and tasting of the New Harvest olive oil , paired with fall apples and pita triangles, followed by a Greek wine tasting and a beautiful Levantine mezza spread. Then, watch beloved Lebanese and Syrian dishes come to life during a live cooking demonstration, followed by a deconstructed buffet where you can build your own plate with a wine pairing of your choice. What We’ll Savor New Harvest EVOO Tasting Learn about Extra-Virgin olive oil from Dame Cary Kelly, an experienced olive oil professional and taste Laconiko's award-winning elixirs, including the first taste of the new harvest. Wine Tasting + Levantine Mezza Enjoy a Greek wine mini-course and tasting alongside Nura’s family style mezza grazing featuring: Hummus Muhammara Olive-Makdous Tapenade Pita bread triangles Pita chips Live Cooking Demo + Deconstructed Buffet Watch a beloved Lebanese & Syrian dish inspired

events.title: From Grief to Becoming: A Guided Meditation for Identity Transitions with Danielle Kean Grassi
events.address: 30 W. Potomac St., Ste 102, Brunswick, MD 21716
events.description: Healing often brings an unexpected kind of grief. As you grow, you may notice yourself letting go of old roles, relationships, beliefs, or ways of coping that once helped you survive. While this transformation can be beautiful, it can also feel uncertain. This 90-minute guided meditation is a deeply reflective, primarily meditative experience designed to support you through that in-between space—not who you once were, but not yet fully who you're becoming. Through grounding practices, breath awareness, nervous system support, visualization, and gentle reflection, you'll be invited to notice what you're carrying, reconnect with your body's wisdom, and cultivate greater capacity for change with compassion. Because everyone's emotional experience is unique, participants are encouraged to move at their own pace. You're always welcome to pause, open your eyes, or simply observe if that feels most supportive. This offering is best suited for those navigating life transitions, personal growth, changing identities, or the emotional experience of becoming someone new. Feel free to bring along a journal and pen for reflection.

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.description: Protect the Health of YOUR Local Forest: Join us at Bacon Ridge Natural Area in Crownsville to spend a morning removing harmful invasive plants from along the trails! Scenic Rivers’ Healthy Forests Program engages community volunteers to help protect the long-term vitality of our largest conservation easement located within Bacon Ridge Natural Area. Our October 2026 workday will focus on vines, shrubs, and grasses. These aggressive invaders threaten vegetation at all levels of the forest from the ground up into the forest canopy. Event Details: Volunteers will be working on designated trail sections to remove specific invasive plant species. Volunteers will be trained in how to identify and remove these plants. Work gloves and tools can be provided by Scenic Rivers, though volunteers are welcome to bring their own gear. To participate, volunteers must: Be 16 years or older to attend without a supervising adult. Volunteers age 10 to 15 may attend with an accompanying adult(s) to supervise work; Be able to hike up to 1 mile to get to designated work areas. Wear long sleeve shirts, long pants, and closed toed shoes. Poison ivy is present in these work areas. Bring a full water bottle. We must have at least 5 registered volunteers for the workday to proceed. So, be sure to invite some friends! Controlling invasive species infestations is a big job and we’ll be happy to have as much help as possible!

events.title: Maryland Emancipation Day
events.address: 8000 Walker Mill Road, Capitol Heights, MD 20743
events.description: What We Carried into Freedom: Knowledge • Skill • Culture • Community Join us at Concord Historic Site for the Maryland Emancipation Day Celebration, an afternoon of living history, music, storytelling, food, family, and community as we commemorate the abolition of slavery in Maryland. Maryland’s Constitution of 1864 took effect on November 1, ending slavery in the state and freeing more than 30,000 African Americans. At Concord—a former tobacco plantation where generations of African Americans were enslaved—Emancipation Day offers an opportunity to remember that history while exploring what freedom made possible. Throughout the afternoon, discover the skills, knowledge, creativity, and cultural traditions African Americans carried through enslavement and used to build lives, families, businesses, institutions, and communities after emancipation. A Celebration Rooted in History Craft Demonstration Area Meet skilled artisans and tradition bearers demonstrating historic and contemporary crafts while discovering the knowledge, creativity, and craftsmanship behind their work. The Griot Sound Stage Experience the power of African American music, storytelling, spoken word, and performance. Inspired by the African tradition of the griot as a keeper of history and community memory, the stage brings stories of culture, freedom, and resilience to life. Hands-On History: Community Glass Project Leave your mark on Concord’s story. Participate in a special, hands-on glass activity connected to the artwork being created for the historic site and learn how community voices are becoming part of Concord’s evolving interpretation. Food Pavilion Take a break, gather around the table, and enjoy food available from participating vendors throughout the celebration.

Valerie Tripp, beloved writer of companion novels for characters like Felicity, Josefina, Samantha, Kit, Molly, Maryellen, and the WellieWishers™, will share her journey as a children’s author. Ms. Tripp will discuss her creative process, inspirations, and experiences bringing these iconic characters to life. The event will conclude with a Q&A session followed by a book signing. Tripp also wrote a STEM series for National Geographic Kids and is the executive editor of the Boys Camp series. She is has adapted classics for Sterling Publishers, and has written numerous leveled readers, songs, stories, nonfiction essays, skills book pages, poems, and plays for educational publishers. Tripp has spoken at The Smithsonian, The New York Historical Society, Mt. events.title: Montgomery County History Conference
events.description: The Montgomery County History Conference Returns November 7! Montgomery College’s Bioscience Education Center on the Germantown Campus This year’s History Conference will open with a keynote by author David O. Stewart, describing the daunting task that the drafters of the Constitution faced in the summer of 1787. Throughout the day, concurrent sessions will cover an interesting variety of topics such as Native American archaeology in Montgomery County, disability rights in Maryland, the history of the FDA, and many more. Anthony Cohen will close the session with reflections on his recent journey called “Freedom Walk 2026,” the 750-mile pilgrimage he took following 19th-century routes to freedom on the Underground Railroad to Canada. As always, your ticket purchase includes a boxed lunch and a catered reception. Join friends and fellow history enthusiasts on November 7 for the Montgomery County History Conference!

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.description: 8 performances | Oct. 31 and Nov. 6*, 7, 13 & 14 at 7:30 p.m. | Nov. 1, 8 & 15 at 2 p.m. Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving, and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four, working in a service job for a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child, but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. Caroline, or Change, produces a valuable theatrical experience that continues to thrill audiences the world over. It is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. events.title: Saint Cecelia Harvest Wine Dinner and Ball
events.description: In the years before a national Thanksgiving Day friends and neighbors would gather for a harvest dinner, giving thanks for the blessings of the year and for the promise of the dawning of the next. These dinners always included social dancing such as the Virginia Reel. Because these celebrations occurred in November they became associated with Saint Cecelia, who in some liturgical calendars was identified as the patron of music. At Shiloh Manor Farm we continue this old Virginia tradition! We are partnering with Magnolias at the Mill to present a tradition Saint Cecelia dinner inspired by a 200 year old book on Virginia cooking authored by one of Patrick Henry’s granddaughters. Following dinner musicians from the Greater Washington Folklore Society will perform traditional English Country Dance tunes that were well known in colonial Virginia such as the Virginia Reel. Dan Gillespie, a highly respected historical dance master will be on hand to teach and call the dances. No experience needed! Comfortable clothing and shoes are a must but we encourage formal or historic attire. A prize will be awarded for best costume!

events.description: Presentation on the Georgetown Branch at 12:30 (appropriate for ages 11 and up): The 11.5 mile branch stretched from just west of Silver Spring, MD across Rock Creek, through Chevy Chase and Bethesda, and along the palisades of the Potomac river into Georgetown in DC. Trains operated from 1892 until 1985 and the line featured a long, tall trestle, a tunnel, and industrial street running. Industries served included cement plants, lumber yards, fuel dealers, three power plants and even a Frito factory. Ben Sullivan will share the colorful history of the line through rare photographs, historic maps, and key stories from its 93-year run. Ongoing Activities: Enjoy train spotting and waving at the engineers, a model layout, a toy train play set, and photos and memorabilia of the railroad’s glory days and historic Silver Spring, plus show off your favorite train-related outfit!

Beyond the joys of eating sourdough bread, many also enjoy the therapeutic nature of a slow, mindful hobby that doubles as a satisfying creative outlet. It's a science experiment you get to eat! events.title: UMD Wind Orchestra Plays Hindemith
events.description: Celebrate the 100th anniversary of Paul Hindemith’s first composition for wind band, Konzertmusik für Blasorchester, and hear other works by Hindemith and Florent Schmitt. Sat Nov 07 8:00pm To – 10:00pm The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center Buy Tickets Clarice website Add to Calendar Celebrate the 100th anniversary of Paul Hindemith’s first work composed for wind band, Konzertmusik für Blasorchester , with the UMD Wind Orchestra! Paul Hindemith is among the most significant German composers of his generation. A proponent for New Objectivity, a style that advocated for public collaboration, engagement and rejection of romantic idealism, Hindemith believed that wind music had been unfairly regarded, and, as a result, premiered Konzertmusik für Blasorchester at the 1926 Donaueschingen Festival. Despite being written “for amateurs,” the piece is complex, drawing on influences from German folk songs and military marches, all with Hindemith’s signature creative melodies and rhythmic energy. This program will also include Hindemith’s Kammermusik No. 1, his first composition in a set of eight chamber music pieces written during the 1920s, as well as Florent Schmitt’s Dionysiaques , a bombastic piece that evokes the ancient Greek festivals honoring the god of wine and dance. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. events.title: Walk in the Woods: Let’s be Smart About Winter Salt ft. Springsong Museum
events.description: Walk with us to discover the impact of winter salt to our waterways & learn more about the Springsong (Rachel Carson) Museum project. Step into the shoes of an environmental detective as we explore the hidden impacts of oversalting our streets and sidewalks during the winter season. Discover how excess salt harms delicate aquatic creatures, disrupts the fragile balance of our ecosystems, and pollutes our drinking water, and learn from the experts about what we can all do to be “winter salt smart.” The walk will also highlight the life and teachings of Silver Spring resident and writer/biologist Rachel Carson (1907-1964), with staff from Springsong Museum on hand to provide rich historical information and examples of Carson’s influential writings. Currently in development, Springsong Museum will transform the vacant building at Burnt Mills East Park into a community museum that connects the public and nature through the wonder and wisdom of Rachel Carson. Join the Izaak Walton League of America on this fun and informative hike to learn about our addiction to deicing salt and how we can all live on a low winter salt diet. Together, we can make a significant difference and create a cleaner, healthier future. Expect to walk a one mile loop on a dirt trail with a bit of rock scrambling at the end. events.title: Weekend Unwind: Sound Bath + Reiki : Saturday Mornings in Falls Church
events.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
events.description: Most people start their Saturday with a list. Groceries, errands, the thing they didn't finish on Friday, still buzzing around in their head. By the time they've “relaxed,” it's Sunday night. Weekend Unwind flips that. Eleven o'clock, one hour, lying down. Crystal singing bowls, a short guided meditation, and Reiki, in a small room with ten people in it and no agenda at all. Nothing to achieve, nothing to be good at. You just lie there and let the week drain out of your shoulders. This class has a different feel from our Thursday night one. Thursday is about switching off. Saturday is slower. People arrive less wound up, settle in faster, and tend to float out rather than rush out. Several regulars come as their standing Saturday thing, the way other people have a standing brunch. It pairs well with brunch afterwards, for the record. If you've never been to a sound bath: you keep your clothes on, you lie on a mat under a blanket, you close your eyes, and I do the rest. The bowls are played around and near you, the sound is physical as much as it is musical, you feel it in your chest, and an hour passes faster than you expect. Everything is provided. Show up in something comfortable with ten minutes to spare, and that's the whole preparation. I'm Victoria Vita. I've been a CPA for over twenty years and a healer for more than seven, and I teach every one of these classes myself. When you come back, and most people do, it's the same room, the same bowls, and the same person. That sameness is kind of the point. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Guests mention the warm welcome, feeling comfortable from the first visit, and booking again — that's the Saturday I try to run. What's included: • 60 minutes of crystal singing bowls, guided meditation and Reiki • Mat, blanket and bolster provided... just bring yourself • Ten spots only, so the room stays quiet and unhurried • A slow finish... no one is hustled out the door at noon Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: Billy Price Band
events.description: 6:00pm • $25 • Tickets on Eventbrite and at the door if still available Billy Price Band Billy Price Band brings soul-blues royalty to Hank Dietle’s Tavern. Price first earned national attention as Roy Buchanan’s vocalist, appearing on Buchanan’s That’s What I’m Here For and Live Stock . Since then, the Pittsburgh singer has built a remarkable catalog spanning 21 albums, CDs, and DVDs—delivering a signature blend of deep soul, blues grit, and first-rate band. His acclaimed collaboration with the late Otis Clay, This Time for Real , won the 2016 Blues Music Award for Best Soul Blues Album. Price has also earned 11 Blues Music Award nominations between 2019 and 2025, received the 2024 Bluebird Reviews Lifetime Career Award in the U.K., and saw his 2024 release Person of Interest nominated for 2025 BMAs in both Soul Blues Album and Album of the Year. Now, Billy returns with the Billy Price Band and their new GetHip release, Random Madness . Recorded in Pittsburgh and released May 1, 2026, the album features 11 new songs co-written by Price and produced by Grammy-winning drummer Tony Braunagel. Backed by Dave Dodd on drums, Tom Valentine on bass, Ian Arthurs on guitar, Jim Britton on keyboards, Eric Spaulding on sax, and Joe Herndon on trumpet, the Billy Price Band brings seasoned musicianship, roaring horns, and irresistible soul-blues energy to one of the area’s most intimate rooms. Order Billy's new album "Random Madness " YouTube • Live @Hank Dietle’s Tavern

events.description: Experiencing history through outdoor mindfulness at Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House. About the Session: The sessions are approximately 90-minutes long and are conducted in relative silence. They include warm-ups, centering, and breathing exercises to connect participants to their bodies and the world around them. These are followed by a walk and an extended sit, which encourages participants to become more fully open and present to their surroundings. We conclude with a returning ritual and a chance to reflect on the experience. This time in nature will not be strenuous; most abilities can be accommodated. All ages are welcome, but children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult. Important Arrival & Check-In Details Check-In Location: All participants must check in at Woodlawn, regardless of session topic. Timing: Sessions start promptly at 12:00 PM (Sundays). events.title: Caroline, or Change the Musical
events.description: 8 performances | October 31 and November 6*, 7, 13, and 14 at 7:30pm | November 1, 8, and 15 at 2:00pm *Friday, November 6 will include ASL interpretation and free tickets for Montgomery County residents! Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

events.title: Cinema Art Bethesda: How to Divorce During the War
events.description: As part of its monthly film screening series, Cinema Art Bethesda is pleased to present Andrius Blaževičius’s award-winning 2026 film. Vilnius, Lithuania, 2022. High-flying executive Marija chooses the worst possible moment to inform her husband Vytas she wants a divorce: just one day before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Suddenly, the couple must navigate the process of separation in tandem with a refugee crisis as well as a mid-life crisis. A struggling film director, Vytas is forced to move in with his Russophile parents, while Marija sees the war impacting both her business and her home life. As the reason for the divorce becomes clear, the dissolution of Marija’s and Vytas’ marriage creates conflicts and opportunities for both of them while also affecting their ever-observant young daughter Dovile. Packed with surprises, Blaževičius’s family drama depicts the fallout of a marriage against the backdrop of extraordinary events with humor and compassion. How to Divorce During the War ( Skyrybos karo metu ) is 1 hour 48 minutes long and in Lithuanian, English, Ukrainian, and Russian with English subtitles. This film is not rated. events.title: Elevated Architecture on the Double
events.description: ELEVATED ARCHITECTURE ON THE DOUBLE Most people walk through Downtown Frederick with absolutely no awareness of what’s happening above their own eyebrows, which is precisely how gargoyles gain confidence. This tour aims to correct that. Many of the defining features of historic Downtown Frederick’s charming architecture are found high above the streets in upper stories, cornices, and spires. Maryland Double Deckers, in partnership with Heritage Frederick, invites you to experience Frederick’s historic buildings on the special Elevated Architecture tour. Discover beautifully preserved examples of commercial, residential, religious, and public buildings displaying major American and European styles that span more than two centuries. Along the way, we’ll explore how the history of Frederick is told by the enduring structures that witnessed it.
