events.title: Food Glorious Food: Class, Culture and Cooking in Colonial Annapolis
events.description: Step back in time and explore the tastes, traditions, and stories that shaped colonial Annapolis! This immersive walking tour reveals how food reflected class, culture, trade, and daily life. Visit three distinctive historic sites: the Waterfront Warehouse, Hogshead Trades Museum, and William Paca House & Garden. Along the way, discover how global trade, local ingredients, social status, and enslavement shaped what Annapolitans ate and how food was prepared and served. Explore the everyday foodways of working and middling residents, the elaborate dining customs of the city’s elite, and the essential labor and culinary knowledge of enslaved people. Enjoy period-inspired tastes and sensory experiences along the way while discovering Annapolis’s past through its kitchens, markets, and tables! Advance registration required; space is limited. Recommended for ages 13+ This event will also be offered at 2:00 pm . Cost: General Admission: $20. Children (13-17), HA Members and Military: $15. The cost includes the Paca Garden admission. Program notes: Please wear comfortable shoes and dress for the weather, as the tour is held rain or shine. The tour route is approximately ¼ miles long and includes elevation changes and uneven walking surfaces. Starts: Waterfront Watehouse 4 Pinkney Street Annapolis MD 20401 Ends: William Paca House & Garden 186 Prince George Street Annapolis, MD 20401 Food Allergy Notice: Food samples will be provided at this program. Some samples may contain gluten and nuts , and cross-contact may occur. Participants with any food allergies or dietary restrictions should use their best judgment before participating and do at their own risk. Accessibility Considerations: Waterfront Warehouse: Accessing this building requires ascending two small steps. There are no restrooms available on site. Hogshead Trades Museum: Accessing this program requires ascending and descending two flights of stairs. There are no restrooms available on site. William Paca House & G

events.title: Fort Tour
events.address: 13551 Fort Washington Road, Fort Washington, MD 20744
events.description: Are you curious about the fascinating history behind Fort Washington? Join us for an enlightening guided tour that delves into the who, what, where, when, and why of this historic fortification! Discover the strategic significance of Digges Point and uncover the reasons it was selected as the ideal site for building the fort. Whether you are a history buff or just looking to enjoy a scenic walk through the fort, this tour is perfect for all ages. Our knowledgeable guides will provide insights into the fort’s construction, its role in defense, and the stories of those who lived and served here. In the event of incliment weather (dangerous heat, thunderstorms, poor air quality, or freezing cold) this program will be moved inside the visitor center and abridge to 30 minutes. If you’re interested in participating but the scheduled times don’t work for you, please don’t hesitate to reach out! Call the Visitor Center at 771-208-1555 or email us prior to your arrival, and we’ll do our best to accommodate your request for a different tour time.

events.title: Habits for Healthy Longevity Virtual Workshop
events.description: The Junior League of Northern Virginia and MantuaHub invite you to an interactive, science-backed session on everyday habits that actually impact how long and how well we live. Drawing on evidence from biomedical research, we'll break down what really drives healthy aging (hint: it's rarely the trendy supplement or the extreme diet) and translate it into practical, sustainable habits you can start this week. In this virtual session, you'll learn: The core pillars of longevity science: movement, sleep, nutrition, stress, and connection Which habits have the strongest evidence behind them Why consistency beats intensity when it comes to health span, not just lifespan Simple ways to build longevity habits into a busy schedule, without overhauling your life How to identify which one or two habits will have the biggest impact for you This isn't a lecture. Expect practical tools and real talk. Date: Saturday, November 14, 2026 Time: 11:00 am to 12:30 pm ET Location: Virtual (Zoom link sent after registration) Cost: Free Who should attend: Anyone who wants to feel good now and stay strong for decades to come. Open to JLNV members and the community. REGISTER NOW About the presenter: Salimah Hussien is the founder of MantuaHub , which brings science-backed wellness education to communities and workplaces across the DMV. events.description: Lez Zeppelin celebrates 50 years of Led Zeppelin at The State Theatre on Saturday, November 14th, 2026. Doors open at 7:00 p.m. with showtime at 8:30 p.m. Founded in 2004 by New York guitarist Steph Paynes, this all-girl quartet has gained unanimous critical acclaim as one of the most exciting live acts around, becoming the first female rock act to pay homage to Led Zeppelin while garnering rave reviews worldwide. Lez Zeppelin stays true to the musically audacious spirit of the original, delivering Led Zeppelin's blistering arrangements and monstrous sound note-for-note at sold-out shows globally. In June 2013, Jimmy Page attended their London show and said of the group: "they played the led zeppelin music with an extraordinary sensuality and an energy and passion that highlighted their superb musicianship." What sets Lez Zeppelin apart is their seamless, unique injection of gender-bending performance into the original material. Featured on major television including BBC, CNN, ABC, CBS, MTV, VH-1, and Fox, plus radio shows like Sirius XM and NPR, their first studio album was produced by legendary Eddie Kramer (Led Zeppelin, Jimi Hendrix). Their second LP, Lez Zeppelin I, authentically remakes Led Zeppelin's debut using the same vintage equipment from 1968. From 40,000-person performances at Times Square to Bonnaroo, Hellfest, and the Isle of Wight, plus twice at Madison Square Garden, Lez Zeppelin has broken both glass and class ceilings. Tickets are $30 advance or $34 day of show. Attendees must be 18 or older to enter unless accompanied by a parent; valid ID is required. Lez Zeppelin offers far more than a tribute—it's a transformative celebration of classic rock excellence at The State Theatre in the Fairfax County area, Virginia. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: NATIONAL PARKS ALONG THE POTOMAC
events.description: What: Four Mile Ranger Guided History Hike from the Carousel in Glen Echo Park to the C&O Canal National Historical Park, Union Arch Bridge and the Clara Barton NHS When: 9:30am Starting Point: The Dentzel Carousel at Glen Echo Park, 7300 MacArthur Blvd. Glen Echo, MD 20812 This two and half hour, four-mile guided hike starts at the Carousel in Glen Echo Park. We will walk through the park and uncover the story of what was once Washington’s premiere amusement park. Next, we will walk a rough downhill trail and cross over the C&O Canal where we will learn about African American canal worker, George Pointer. We will then walk up-stream before crossing the canal again and ascending the hill to learn about the Union Arch Bridge, part of the Washington Aqueduct. Finally, we will stroll through the town of Glen Echo to Clara Barton National Historic Site (NHS) where we will discover the history of the house and the story of its famous resident, the founder of the American Red Cross, Clara Barton. Called a voice for this historic moment (The Washington Post), bass-baritone Will Liverman joins the orchestra for the world premiere of Sniders Urge, an NSO co-commission setting texts by poet Tracy K. Smith. Stravinskys Symphonies of Wind Instruments distills music to spare, haunting phrases, while Thomas Street Song draws on the rhythms and sounds of the city. Tchaikovskys Serenade for Strings brings the evening to a warm and celebratory close. There is a ticket limit of 8 tickets per person and per credit card on this event.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Seth Walker
events.description: Seth Walker brings his soulful blend of Blues, Americana, and Roots music to the stage with the easy groove and gospel‑rich vocals that have made him a standout in today’s roots scene. Currently celebrating his new album Why The Worry, Walker leans into a philosophy of ease and authenticity, channeling influences from JJ Cale to Bill Withers and Al Green. The album reunites him with longtime collaborators and features a mix of originals and carefully chosen covers that reflect resilience, warmth, and a renewed musical clarity. Praised by NPR, American Songwriter, and The Washington Post, Walker has toured with The Mavericks, The Wood Brothers, Raul Malo, and Ruthie Foster. His songwriting continues to reach new audiences, including “Moon and Stars,” the title track of The Mavericks’ recent album. With twelve albums, a signature blend of melody and groove, and a sound that feels both timeless and freshly inspired, Seth Walker offers an unforgettable live experience, equal parts soulful, uplifting, and deeply human.

events.title: Sweet Dreams: Mandy Barnett Sings Patsy Cline
events.description: “Sweet Dreams” is a stunning tribute to the timeless music of Patsy Cline. The concert features a collection of iconic classic country songs originally recorded by Patsy Cline, including “Crazy,” “Sweet Dreams,” “Walking After Midnight,” “I Fall to Pieces,” “Always,” “Faded Love,” “She’s Got You,” “Strange,” and many more. Widely considered Nashville’s finest vocalist, Mandy Barnett rose to prominence at the age of 18 after being chosen among 400 auditionees by the legendary Ryman Auditorium for the title role in the 1994 musical production of Always… Patsy Cline . Her successful performance as Patsy Cline garnered tremendous press, both domestic and international, establishing the production as a staple of American theater. An official member of the Grand Ole Opry since 2021, Mandy has performed on more than 400 occasions, sharing the stage with legendary performers including Dolly Parton, Ringo Starr, Kristin Chenoweth, Pat Benatar, Judy Collins, Connie Stevens, Garth Brooks, and Michael Feinstein, among numerous others. Learn more about “Sweet Dreams” and Mandy Barnett by visiting her official website. This show is part of the Weinberg Center’s Centennial Events, celebrating 100 years of entertainment in our historic building. The Weinberg Center , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers a historic backdrop and timeless atmosphere for a meaningful entertainment experience.

What will the universe be like in "deep time"? Completely empty (or full of dark energy) or will it collapse down to a "big crunch" or neither? events.title: Unfossilizing African Art
events.description: Presented after extensive research, this exhibition recontextualizes African material culture objects held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. events.title: YOUR Body in Yoga: A Functional Anatomy Weekend with Machelle Lee
events.address: 30 W. Potomac St., Ste 102, Brunswick, MD 21716
events.description: Harshly judging one's range of motion is one of the greatest sources of unnecessary suffering in many people’s yoga practice. The poses in yoga are intended to be a method to move the regenerative and healing life force. To do that effectively in yoga, we must understand each of our own (or our students) unique structures and explore when we can move more deeply into a posture or when to acknowledge limitations with respect. Although some restrictions in range of motion are related to tight muscles, and more are related to contracted fascia and ligaments, many significant limitations are actually due to variations in bone shapes and joint orientations that can differ dramatically from one person to the next. Understanding YOUR yoga anatomy is best learned through direct hands-on experience - testing your bones/joints and witnessing them curiously and compassionately to the bones of others. This functional, comparative anatomy workshop explores the 14 major joint segments of the body that account for most of our yoga postures. For each joint intersection, we will perform bone analysis and range of motion tests on ourselves, compare with each other, and demonstrate how each varying joints will express itself in specific yoga postures. 12 CEUs Available for Yoga Teachers with Yoga Alliance Anatomy is a vast subject, but this interactive workshop reveals the basics in a way that clarifies and simplifies the yoga practice - putting the attention back where it belongs - how the key action of each pose makes you FEEL and moves the life force. In this workshop, participants often experience an “ah-ha” moment about their body and their practice, which can be powerfully liberating and self-accepting. This workshop is ideal for all yoga practitioners, whether one is a beginner or experienced student wishing to deepen their knowledge of their body in practice and for yoga teachers looking to expand their teaching and cueing.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape.Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available.Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape.Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available.Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

The Carol Stuart Watson Collection is now available for public research in the Peabody Room at Georgetown Neighborhood Library. Make an appointment to view the collection. events.description: Experiencing history through outdoor mindfulness at Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House. About the Session: The sessions are approximately 90-minutes long and are conducted in relative silence. They include warm-ups, centering, and breathing exercises to connect participants to their bodies and the world around them. These are followed by a walk and an extended sit which encourages participants to become more fully open and present to their surroundings. We conclude with a returning ritual and a chance to reflect on the experience. This time in nature will not be strenuous; most abilities can be accommodated. All ages are welcomed but children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult. Important Arrival & Check-In Details Check-In Location: All participants must check in at Woodlawn, regardless of session topic. Timing: Sessions start promptly at 12:00 PM (Sundays). Please arrive early to ensure a timely start. Duration: Approximately 90 minutes. Fall Schedule & Locations Sunday, October 11 | Woodlawn Sunday, October 25 | Pope-Leighey House Sunday, November 1 | Woodlawn Sunday, November 8 | Pope-Leighey House Tickets & Policies Price: $30 per ticket. events.description: Did you know that part of the Washington-Rochambeau Revolutionary Route National Historic Trail passes through Prince William Forest Park? Take a hike through history at Prince William Forest Park on the Crossing Trail, which follows part of the route where, in 1781, General Rochambeau's French Army and General Washington's Continental Army marched troops south from New York to fight the British Army in Yorktown, VA during the Revolutionary War. Celebrate the 250th anniversary of American Independence by following in the footsteps of these armies as you learn about travel in the 1700s along this one and a half mile trail. Bring water and bug spray on this mostly shaded one and a half hour hike.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape. Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available. Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Explore a little-known part of the park and tour a cabin camp built in the 1930s. Join park rangers at Cabin Camp 2 at Prince William Forest Park to learn more about the period of the park’s history in the 1940s when the Office of Strategic Services (OSS) trained spies in the park. Hikes are limited to 30 visitors each and first-come, first-serve free tickets for the hike will be available at the event at Cabin Camp 2 starting at 8:30am. Unfortunately, the off-trail hike is inaccessible to wheelchairs and strollers. It is recommended to wear long pants and hiking shoes if planning to do the off-trail hike. Guided cabin camp tours are offered to visitors after each hike and are open to all visitors. Visitors are also welcome to do a self-guided tour of the cabin camp anytime between 8:30am and 3:00pm. The cabin camp gates will close at 3:00pm.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape.Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available.Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Lace up your hiking boots and follow in the footsteps of Theodore Roosevelt, the adventurous president who believed that time spent in nature built character, courage, and a stronger nation. Beginning at Peirce Mill, this 1.5-mile (round-trip) guided hike winds through scenic trails and rugged landscapes that Roosevelt explored while escaping the pressures of the presidency. This hike covers uneven, tight, rocky terrain with steep elevation changes and may be challenging for some visitors. Participants should wear sturdy footwear, bring water, and dress appropriately for the weather. Recommended for ages 10 and older. Children must be accompanied by an adult.

events.description: Join a National Park Service ranger for a guided walk-through Battleground National Cemetery to explore Civil War monuments, their symbols, and the stories they were built to preserve. Discover how art, memory, and history come together in this quiet landscape where Washington, DC’s past is written in stone. As a part of the Freedom 250 commemoration, this program invites visitors to reflect on sacrifice, citizenship, and the enduring power of public memory. Please note that parking is limited to public streets.
